sourceNote.title: Checkout address form
sourceNote.html:
Checkout shipping address

Testing the new shipping address step in a demo web shop (staging build 2.4.0).

  • Fields: full name, street and number, postcode, city, country (dropdown, NL/BE/DE).

  • Postcode format depends on country: NL is 4 digits + 2 letters (1234 AB, space optional), BE and DE are 4 and 5 digits.

  • Name max 60 characters; street max 100.

  • Continue button is disabled until all required fields are filled. Errors show inline under the field after leaving it.

  • Changing country after typing a postcode re-validates the postcode.

  • Observed: pasting a postcode with a trailing space for NL showed an error, typing the same value did not.

  • Observed: the address is kept when going back from payment to shipping.

bodyHtml:
Feature: Checkout shipping address step (demo web shop, staging build 2.4.0)

Scope: Fields full name, street and number, postcode, city, and country (dropdown: NL/BE/DE). The scenarios cover postcode rules per country, maximum field lengths, enabling the Continue button, inline errors, re-validation when the country changes, pasted versus typed input, and keeping the address when going back from payment.

Scenario: Postcode validation per country

Test case: Valid NL postcode is accepted with and without a space

Purpose: Check that NL postcodes in the format 4 digits + 2 letters are accepted, with the space optional.

Preconditions: Shopper is on the shipping address step of the checkout in staging build 2.4.0.

Test data: Country NL; postcodes "1234 AB" and "1234AB".

Given the shopper has selected country NL

When they enter a postcode in the format 4 digits + 2 letters, with or without a space, and leave the field

Then no inline error is shown under the postcode field

  • Select NL in the country dropdown.

  • Type "1234 AB" in the postcode field and leave the field.

  • Check that no inline error appears under the postcode field.

  • Replace the value with "1234AB" and leave the field.

  • Check that no inline error appears under the postcode field.

Expected result: Both values are accepted for NL.

Coverage notes: Positive case. Covers the optional space in the NL format.

Test case: Invalid NL postcode shows an inline error

Purpose: Check that NL postcodes that break the 4 digits + 2 letters format are rejected.

Preconditions: Shopper is on the shipping address step with country NL selected.

Test data: "123 AB" (3 digits), "12345 AB" (5 digits), "1234 A" (1 letter), "1234" (no letters).

Given the shopper has selected country NL

When they enter a postcode that does not match 4 digits + 2 letters and leave the field

Then an inline error is shown under the postcode field

  • Select NL in the country dropdown.

  • For each test data value, type it in the postcode field and leave the field.

  • Check that an inline error appears under the postcode field for each value.

Expected result: Each invalid value gets an inline error under the postcode field after the shopper leaves it.

Coverage notes: Negative and boundary case. Tests one digit and one letter fewer or more than the NL format allows.

Test case: BE and DE postcode digit length boundaries

Purpose: Check that BE accepts 4-digit postcodes and DE accepts 5-digit postcodes, and that other lengths are rejected.

Preconditions: Shopper is on the shipping address step.

Test data: BE: "1000" (valid), "100" and "10000" (invalid). DE: "10115" (valid), "1011" and "101150" (invalid).

Given the shopper has selected country BE or DE

When they enter a postcode with the required number of digits, or one digit fewer or more, and leave the field

Then only the value with the correct number of digits is accepted without an inline error

  • Select BE, enter "1000" and leave the field. Check that no error appears.

  • Enter "100" and then "10000", leaving the field after each one. Check that an inline error appears each time.

  • Select DE, enter "10115" and leave the field. Check that no error appears.

  • Enter "1011" and then "101150", leaving the field after each one. Check that an inline error appears each time.

Expected result: BE accepts exactly 4 digits and DE accepts exactly 5 digits. Other lengths show an inline error.

Coverage notes: Boundary and negative cases for BE and DE. The note does not say whether letters or spaces are allowed for BE or DE, so those inputs are not covered.

Test case: Changing the country re-validates an entered postcode

Purpose: Check that the postcode is re-validated when the country changes after a postcode has been typed.

Preconditions: Shopper is on the shipping address step.

Test data: Postcode "1234 AB" with NL, then BE and DE. Postcode "10115" with DE, then NL.

Given the shopper has entered a postcode that is valid for the selected country

When they change the country to one where that postcode is not valid

Then the postcode is re-validated and an inline error is shown under the postcode field

  • Select NL, enter "1234 AB" and leave the field. Check that no error appears.

  • Change the country to BE. Check that the postcode is re-validated and an error appears.

  • Change the country to DE. Check that the postcode is re-validated and an error appears.

  • Select DE, enter "10115" and leave the field. Check that no error appears.

  • Change the country to NL. Check that the postcode is re-validated and an error appears.

Expected result: Every country change re-validates the postcode against the new country's format.

Coverage notes: State transition between countries. A useful extra check is going from an invalid to a valid combination, for example "1000" entered with DE and then the country changed to BE, to see the error clear.

Test case: Pasted and typed NL postcode with a trailing space are validated the same way

Purpose: Re-check the observation that a pasted NL postcode with a trailing space showed an error, while typing the same value did not.

Preconditions: Shopper is on the shipping address step with country NL selected. The test data value is on the clipboard.

Test data: "1234 AB " (with a trailing space).

Given the shopper has selected country NL

When they first type and then paste "1234 AB " into the postcode field, leaving the field each time

Then both input methods give the same validation result

  • Type "1234 AB " (with a trailing space) in the postcode field and leave the field. Note the validation result.

  • Clear the field.

  • Paste "1234 AB " (with a trailing space) in the postcode field and leave the field. Note the validation result.

  • Compare the two results.

Expected result: Typed and pasted input are validated the same way. The note observed a difference: the pasted value showed an error and the typed value did not.

Coverage notes: Evidence-preserving case based on an observation in the note. The note does not say whether a trailing space should be valid, so the intended outcome needs confirming.

Scenario: Field length limits

Test case: Full name maximum of 60 characters

Purpose: Check the 60-character limit on the full name field.

Preconditions: Shopper is on the shipping address step.

Test data: Names of 59, 60 and 61 characters.

Given the shopper is filling in the full name field

When they enter names of 59, 60 and 61 characters and leave the field

Then 59 and 60 characters are accepted, and 61 characters are not accepted

  • Enter a 59-character name and leave the field. Check that no error appears.

  • Enter a 60-character name and leave the field. Check that no error appears.

  • Enter a 61-character name and leave the field. Check that the value is truncated, blocked or flagged with an inline error.

Expected result: The name is limited to 60 characters.

Coverage notes: Boundary case. The note does not say how values over the limit are handled (blocked input or an inline error), so record what you observe.

Test case: Street and number maximum of 100 characters

Purpose: Check the 100-character limit on the street and number field.

Preconditions: Shopper is on the shipping address step.

Test data: Street values of 99, 100 and 101 characters.

Given the shopper is filling in the street and number field

When they enter values of 99, 100 and 101 characters and leave the field

Then 99 and 100 characters are accepted, and 101 characters are not accepted

  • Enter a 99-character street and leave the field. Check that no error appears.

  • Enter a 100-character street and leave the field. Check that no error appears.

  • Enter a 101-character street and leave the field. Check that the value is truncated, blocked or flagged with an inline error.

Expected result: The street and number is limited to 100 characters.

Coverage notes: Boundary case. Handling of values over the limit is not specified in the note.

Scenario: Form completion and inline errors

Test case: Continue stays disabled until all required fields are filled

Purpose: Check that the Continue button is enabled only after all required fields are filled.

Preconditions: Shopper is on the shipping address step with an empty form.

Test data: Full name "Test Shopper", street and number "Teststraat 1", postcode "1234 AB", city "Amsterdam", country NL.

Given the shipping address form is empty

When the shopper fills in the required fields one at a time

Then Continue stays disabled until the last required field is filled, and is then enabled

  • Check that Continue is disabled on the empty form.

  • Fill in the fields one at a time, checking after each one that Continue is still disabled while any required field is empty.

  • Fill in the last required field and check that Continue becomes enabled.

  • Clear one required field and check that Continue is disabled again.

Expected result: Continue is disabled until all required fields are filled.

Coverage notes: Positive and negative case. The note does not list which fields are required, so confirm that before running this case.

Test case: Inline error appears under the field after leaving it

Purpose: Check when and where validation errors are shown.

Preconditions: Shopper is on the shipping address step with country NL selected.

Test data: Postcode "12AB".

Given the shopper is typing an invalid postcode

When they leave the postcode field

Then an inline error appears directly under the postcode field

  • Type "12AB" in the postcode field without leaving it. Check whether an error is shown while typing.

  • Leave the field by moving focus to another field.

  • Check that an inline error appears under the postcode field.

Expected result: The error appears inline under the field once the shopper leaves it.

Coverage notes: Covers when errors are triggered and where they are placed.

Scenario: Navigation between checkout steps

Test case: Address is kept when going back from payment to shipping

Purpose: Check that the entered address is kept when the shopper goes back from the payment step.

Preconditions: Shopper has filled in a valid shipping address.

Test data: Full name "Test Shopper", street and number "Teststraat 1", postcode "1234 AB", city "Amsterdam", country NL.

Given the shopper has completed the shipping address step and is on the payment step

When they go back to the shipping step

Then all address fields still contain the values they entered

  • Fill in all fields with the test data and select Continue.

  • On the payment step, go back to the shipping step.

  • Check that full name, street and number, postcode, city and country still have the entered values.

  • Check that Continue is enabled.

Expected result: The address is kept, as the note observed.

Coverage notes: Regression check for an observed behavior. Repeating it with BE and DE addresses would also cover country-specific data.
